48191.subject: Technical Drawing
48191.question_text:
Using the appropriate drawing instruments, construct a perfect circle of diameter $50 \text{ mm}$ and label the following parts:
Centre, Radius, Diameter, Circumference.
48191.explanation:
1. Place the compass needle at the centre point of the circle.
2. Adjust the compass to a radius of $25 \text{ mm}$ (half of $50 \text{ mm}$).
3. Draw the circle by rotating the compass $360^\circ$.
4. Label the centre point as Centre.
5. Draw a line from the centre to the circumference and label it Radius ($25 \text{ mm}$).
6. Draw a line passing through the centre and touching the circumference at both ends, label it Diameter ($50 \text{ mm}$).
7. Label the entire curved line as Circumference.

48192.subject: Technical Drawing
48192.question_text: Which of the following is the standard size for an A3 drawing sheet in millimetres?
48192.explanation: The standard size for an A3 drawing sheet is $297 \text{ mm} \times 420 \text{ mm}$, as defined by the ISO 216 standard.

48193.subject: Technical Drawing
48193.question_text:
Draw a title block of dimensions $180 \text{ mm} \times 50 \text{ mm}$ at the bottom right corner of an A4 sheet. Include the following details:
Name, Index Number, School, Date, Scale, and Drawing Title.
48193.explanation:
1. Draw a rectangle of $180 \text{ mm} \times 50 \text{ mm}$ at the bottom right corner of the sheet.
2. Divide the title block into sections for:
  - Drawing Title (top-left, bold)
  - Name and Index Number (middle-left)
  - School (middle-right)
  - Date (bottom-left)
  - Scale (bottom-right).
3. Ensure all text is in uppercase and legible, using standard lettering techniques.

48194.subject: Technical Drawing
48194.question_text: Which line type is used to represent hidden edges in an orthographic projection?
48194.explanation: A dashed line (medium thickness) is used to represent hidden edges in orthographic projections, as per standard technical drawing conventions.

48195.subject: Technical Drawing
48195.question_text: Construct a perpendicular bisector of a line segment $AB$ of length $60 \text{ mm}$ using only a compass and straightedge. Label all construction lines and points.
48195.explanation:
1. Draw line segment $AB = 60 \text{ mm}$.
2. With $A$ as centre, draw an arc of radius $> 30 \text{ mm}$ above and below $AB$.
3. With $B$ as centre, draw arcs of the same radius to intersect the previous arcs at points $C$ and $D$.
4. Draw a straight line through $C$ and $D$ to intersect $AB$ at $M$.
5. $CM$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, and $M$ is the midpoint.
6. Label all points and construction lines.

48196.subject: Technical Drawing
48196.question_text: Construct a regular hexagon with side length $30 \text{ mm}$ using the circumscribed circle method. Show all construction lines and label the vertices.
48196.explanation:
1. Draw a circle of radius $30 \text{ mm}$ (since the side length of a regular hexagon equals its circumradius).
2. Mark a point $A$ on the circumference.
3. Using the same radius, step off points $B, C, D, E,$ and $F$ around the circumference.
4. Join the points $A$ to $F$ to form the hexagon.
5. Label all vertices and construction lines.

48197.subject: Technical Drawing
48197.question_text:
Given the front elevation and plan of a block, draw the end elevation using first-angle orthographic projection. Include all hidden details.
(Assume dimensions are provided in a diagram.)
48197.explanation:
1. Identify the front elevation and plan views.
2. Project lines from the front elevation and plan to determine the height and depth of the end elevation.
3. Use dashed lines to represent hidden edges.
4. Ensure all dimensions and features align correctly in the end elevation.
5. Label the views as Front Elevation, Plan, and End Elevation.

48198.subject: Technical Drawing
48198.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the internal features of a symmetrical object by cutting through half of it?
48198.explanation: A half section is used to show the internal features of a symmetrical object by cutting through half of it, allowing both internal and external details to be visible.

48199.subject: Technical Drawing
48199.question_text: Draw an isometric view of a cube with side length $40 \text{ mm}$. Include all visible edges and label the isometric axes.
48199.explanation:
1. Draw the isometric axes at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal.
2. Mark a point $O$ as the origin.
3. From $O$, measure $40 \text{ mm}$ along each axis to locate the vertices of the cube.
4. Complete the cube by drawing the remaining edges parallel to the axes.
5. Label the axes as X, Y, and Z.
6. Ensure all lines are drawn to scale and visible edges are continuous.

48200.subject: Technical Drawing
48200.question_text: Develop the lateral surface of a right circular cylinder of diameter $50 \text{ mm}$ and height $70 \text{ mm}$. Show all construction lines and label the dimensions.
48200.explanation:
1. Calculate the circumference of the cylinder: $C = \pi d = \pi \times 50 \text{ mm} = 157.08 \text{ mm}$ (approx).
2. Draw a rectangle of height $70 \text{ mm}$ and length $157.08 \text{ mm}$.
3. Divide the rectangle into equal parts (e.g., 12) to represent the unfolded surface.
4. Label the height as $70 \text{ mm}$ and the length as $157.08 \text{ mm}$.
5. Show construction lines for the divisions and label the development as Lateral Surface Development.
